title: Pravasi Trust Urges Kerala to Tap NRI Savings for High-Speed Rail Project
excerpt: A Pravasi trust has submitted a memorandum to Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan proposing tax-free bonds to channel Non-Resident Keralite savings toward a high-speed railway linking Thiruvananthapuram and Kasaragod.
body:
• A Pravasi trust has submitted a memorandum to Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan proposing that NRI savings fund the state's proposed high-speed railway between Thiruvananthapuram and Kasaragod.
  • The trust suggests raising funds through secured, redeemable, and tax-free non-convertible bonds aimed at Non-Resident Keralites.
  • Kerala has a long history of mobilizing diaspora capital for infrastructure, including the KSFE Pravasi Chitty scheme that has channeled over ₹1,000 crore into KIIFB bonds.
  • The proposal taps into an estimated $15 billion in annual NRI remittances to Kerala, the highest per capita among Indian states.

A Pravasi trust has called on the Kerala government to tap into the savings of Non-Resident Keralites to fund the state's ambitious high-speed railway project, according to The Hindu. In a memorandum submitted to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, the trust proposed raising capital through secured, redeemable, and tax-free non-convertible bonds for the planned high-speed rail corridor between Thiruvananthapuram and Kasaragod.

The Bond Proposal

The trust's memorandum outlines a financial instrument specifically designed to attract NRI investors — a tax-free non-convertible bond that would be both secured against state infrastructure assets and redeemable after a fixed term. The structure aims to offer NRKs (Non-Resident Keralites) a safe, government-backed investment while providing the state with long-term capital for one of its most expensive infrastructure undertakings.

The Thiruvananthapuram-Kasaragod high-speed rail corridor, spanning roughly 530 kilometers across the length of Kerala, is among the state's priority infrastructure projects. The project requires massive capital investment, and traditional funding sources have been under strain.

Kerala's NRI Fundraising Track Record

Kerala has a well-established track record of channeling diaspora money into development. The Kerala State Financial Enterprises (KSFE) launched the Pravasi Chitty scheme in 2018, a savings-cum-investment product designed specifically for NRIs. The scheme, which operates fully online, has attracted subscribers from the UAE, Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Europe.

All proceeds from Pravasi Chitty are invested in bonds issued by the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB), the state government's primary vehicle for mobilizing long-term development capital. KIIFB has channeled these funds into roads, bridges, schools, hospitals, IT parks, and drinking water projects across the state. Over ₹1,000 crore worth of KIIFB bonds have been subscribed through Pravasi Chitty to date, according to Kerala Calling, the state government's official publication.

"By enrolling into this scheme, expats will receive benefits like insurance, pension. All processes can be done online."

— Peelipose Thomas, former KSFE Chairman

The NRI Capital Pool

Kerala's NRI community represents one of the largest diaspora capital pools of any Indian state. An estimated 2.1 million Keralites live abroad, primarily in Gulf Cooperation Council countries, with significant populations also in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia. NRI remittances to Kerala are estimated at over $15 billion annually, accounting for a substantial share of the state's economy.

The trust's proposal aims to redirect a portion of these savings from private consumption and real estate into productive state infrastructure, offering returns competitive with commercial bank deposits while funding projects that benefit the communities NRIs maintain ties with.

Challenges and Precedents

While the concept of NRI-funded infrastructure bonds is not new in India — the Reserve Bank of India and the central government have periodically offered NRI bond schemes — Kerala's approach is distinctive in its state-level focus and the direct link between investor funds and specific projects. Subscribers to the existing Pravasi Chitty scheme can choose which development categories their money supports, from coastal roads to cultural complexes.

The high-speed rail proposal, however, would represent a significantly larger financial commitment than existing schemes. Questions around project timeline, cost overruns, and the regulatory framework for state-issued tax-free bonds would need resolution before any fundraising could begin.

What's Next

The memorandum is now with Chief Minister Satheesan's office. Whether the government will formally adopt the bond proposal or integrate it into existing KIIFB frameworks remains to be seen. For the millions of Keralites abroad, the proposal represents both an investment opportunity and a chance to directly shape the infrastructure of their home state.
nri_angle: Directly proposes channeling NRI savings into Kerala infrastructure, offering diaspora Keralites a government-backed investment tied to their home state's development.
